newsitem.title: NORWAY: Goldman Sachs sees UNI share rising.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs sees UNI share rising.

text.p: Norwegian insurance group UNI Storebrand is a market outperformer whose stock price should rise by about 30 percent to 46.8 crowns in the next 16 months, according to Goldman Sachs.
In an analysis dated August 30, the investment bank noted that UNI is Norway's largest insurer, leader both in life and non-life where it holds 30 percent and 40 percent of the market respectively.

"We initiate coverage of UNI Storebrand with a Market Outperformer rating and a 1997 year-end target price of 46.8 crowns, representing a total return of 32 percent in 16 months from the current price of 35.3 crowns," it said.
UNI traded at 35.7 crowns on Thursday afternoon.

"The shares are currently trading at a 10 percent discount to current embedded value," it said. "This compares with premiums of 15 percent and 36 percent respectively for Skandia and Trygg-Hansa in Sweden.

"We believe that the shares, with a ROE above 10 percent even during a downturn, deserve to trade at a small premium to current book value or, equivalently, in line with the 1997 year-end book value."
The analysis noted that the Norwegian parliament were now discussing new regulatory framework for life business that should be positive for life insurers.
Following a financial crisis in 1992, UNI is now comfortably capitalised, it said.
Having achieved a higher level of solvency, management has implemented major measures to improve efficiency and reduce costs, mostly in the non-life area, it said.
"These measures should partially offset the deterioration in the claims ratio that is taking place in 1996-1997 due to the worsening of the Norwegian non-life cycle," Goldman Sachs said.
